correctness.rationale: For every \(p,q\), exact Laplacian multiplication yields two degree-scaled independent-Gaussian coordinate blocks plus common Gaussian sums. The joint max/min extreme-value limit follows from the explicitly displayed product probability, and the common sums are negligible at scale \(s_n\asymp n/\sqrt{\log n}\). Independent Gumbel competition gives an exactly logistic winning mark, independent of the winning value. Haar radial normalization gives an \(o_{\Pr}(1)\) perturbation after scaling. Within-block automorphism symmetry identifies cone angles with vertex-selection probabilities; three direct squared-distance formulas prove near-equilateral geometry. The full joint theorem, quantifiers and Euclidean embedding were reviewed; finite tests only check the exact support algebra and illustrate the asymptotics.

value.rationale: The distribution of supporting graph-vertex classes is a canonical normal-cone measure of the Euclidean Laplacian simplex. Vanishing relative distortion of every edge length fails to prevent an order-one, logarithmically amplified cone-mass bias. The theorem supplies the complete finite-parameter logistic crossover and its independent joint Gumbel width law, a meaningful stability boundary for a natural graph-polytope family rather than a chosen numerical slice.
